data.name: Madhusudan
data.gender_notes: Madhusudan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Madhu means nectar or sweet, and sudan means one who subdues or calms. This name is given to a child believed to have the ability to soothe and pacify others with their sweet nature. The name Madhusudan carries the meaning “Sweet or nectar-filled one” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Madhusudan usually hope their child will grow to embody sweet or nectar-filled one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the calming and soothing nature of Lord Vishnu.
data.etymology: Madhusudan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sweet or nectar-filled one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Madhusudan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Madhusudan is a revered name among Hindus, associated with various gods, particularly Lord Krishna, who is also known by this name. The title is also given to other Hindu deities like Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu. In many Hindu epics and folktales, this name symbolizes wisdom, courage, and the power to subdue worldly desires.
data.spiritual_significance: Madhusudan carries deep spiritual significance as it represents the divine power to subdue one's inner desires and cravings. This name signifies a calm and composed individual who has achieved mastery over their senses, which ultimately leads to a higher level of spiritual awareness and wisdom. It also represents the power to provide inner peace and solace to others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Madhusudan: Slayer of the demon Madhu, symbolizing the victory of good over evil, and the supreme intoxication of self-realization through devotion to God (Bhagavan Vishnu).

vedic_reference.note: This name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'madhu' meaning 'honey' and 'sudan' meaning 'one who gives'. It is the name of Lord Vishnu in his form as the slayer of the demon Madhu. He is also known as Madhava and Matsya Avatar. The name is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures including the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Madhusudan remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
